statuses.title: lr_schedule is compare=False, so the accountant's structural merge collapses MF processes with different schedules
statuses.note: Fixed by 4bfd0c16 (fix(accounting): preserve schedule identity during composition, #883) via the third option in the OPQ fix sketch: DpProcess.__or__ no longer merges by dataclass equality. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:396-416 adds _repeated_pld_cache_key/_has_same_repeated_pld, and :503 and :511 replace `left_leaf == right_leaf` / `r_leaf == right_leaf` with _has_same_repeated_pld(..., merged_count), which compares Repeated(leaf, count)._pld_cache_key(); those keys go through strategy_cache_key -> materialize_schedule (_schedule_fingerprint.py:14-21, 36-46), which evaluates the schedule at every step in [0, n_steps). Verified on the OPQ's own scenario (b) and beyond, at n_steps=64, bands=4, momentum=0.9: b_min_sep with linear vs exponential schedules gives eps 1.11657 vs 1.13009 and `pa|pb`, `pb|pa`, `pa|none` all return Composed (1.35368), never Repeated; the identical pair `pa|pa` still collapses to Repeated (1.34701), so the optimisation is not lost; the right-spine path ((blt|pa)|pb) and the CachedProcess path also return Composed for differing schedules and Repeated for identical ones. Same result for the cyclic-Poisson amplifier. Scenario (a) is now unreachable by a stronger route: LambdaCgdStrategy.__post_init__ (_lambda_cgd.py:111-121) and BisrStrategy.__post_init__ (_bisr.py:645-655) reject any non-None lr_schedule outright. CAVEAT, not filed as a finding because I could find no path where it changes a number: the four strategies still declare lr_schedule with compare=False (_band_mf.py:114, _blt.py:133, _bisr.py:642, _lambda_cgd.py:109), so `pa == pb` is still True for two processes with different epsilon. I checked the places that could bite - PLD caching keys on _pld_cache_key not __eq__; the BandMF/BLT coefficient lru_caches key on the materialized lr_key tuple (_band_mf.py:72-78, _blt.py:65-73), not on the strategy object; and trainer resume compares the serialized horizon_process_state (which carries the schedule recipe) as drift="dp_relevant" (_checkpoint.py:272-275) - so the residual is an API wart, not a live miscount.

statuses.title: BISR keeps n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers, contradicting the documented p-1-vector design
statuses.note: Rewritten by d09d7b9a (fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth, #886) into a direct signed FIR convolution over a bounded newest-first ring: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:321-408 _direct_bisr_streaming_matrix, with window = len(inverse_coefficients) - 1 where inverse = strategy._inv_coefs()[:n_steps] (so min(p, n_steps)-1 buffers), effective_taps = column_scales[step] * inv[:count+1] at :379-383 and next_history = (iid_noise, *state.history[:window-1]) at :399. _make_bisr_noise (:586-592) now builds that operator instead of inverse_as_streaming_matrix(bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps)). NUMERICAL EQUIVALENCE (the task's specific ask): I ran the public mf_gaussian_noise path against the dense forward-substitution reference (BisrStrategy.streaming_matrix(n_steps=...) driven through _streaming_mf_noise with the same key, so both consume the identical iid stream) over 418 configurations - bandwidth in {2,3,4,6,12}, n_steps in {1,2,3,5,8,13,32,64,129,256}, normalized in {True,False}, momentum in {0.0,0.5,0.9,0.99}, plus three signed/non-monotone custom inv_coefficients sets ((1,-0.5,0.25), (2,-1,0.5,-0.25), (1,0.3,-0.7,0.2,0.1)) at n in {4,16,64}. findings.title: IdentityStrategy.sensitivity ignores the participation schema, so bare mf_gaussian under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k) - the one sibling the participation-schema fix did not convert
findings.claim: Commit e44d6ab6 (fix(dpftrl): honour the participation schema in BandMF sensitivity, #998) converted MfStrategy.sensitivity from a single-participation column norm into a schema-aware quantity and updated BandMF accordingly, and BLT/BSR/BISR/lambda-CGD already honoured the schema. IdentityStrategy was left as `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float: return 1.0`, which swallows min_sep and max_participations entirely. MfGaussian.pld (_mf_gaussian.py:132-141) feeds exactly that value to _native.mf_gaussian_pld as the sensitivity of the whole bare release, so a bare identity MF process with a declared multi-participation schema is priced as if each protected unit contributed once. For C = I the correct L2 sensitivity over a participation pattern pi is ||sum_{j in pi} e_j|| = sqrt(k), not 1. The same commit's new MfStrategy protocol docstring (types.py:55-59) actively blesses the exemption: "A strategy whose sensitivity is genuinely participation-independent may ignore the schema and document that it does; IdentityStrategy returns 1.0 unconditionally on that basis" - which is false under the schema-sensitivity definition the neighbouring sentences use. The API fails open: it returns a number rather than refusing, and mf_gaussian's own docstring (_mf_gaussian.py:169-171) documents min_sep/max_participations as bare-use participation bounds with no caveat.
findings.failure_scenario: A user accounts an unamplified MF run with the identity encoder and five participations at least 100 steps apart over a 1000-step horizon: `fa.mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5)` returns 4.37717809602987. The mechanism actually run releases a sum whose sensitivity is sqrt(5)*C, i.e. an effective multiplier of 1/sqrt(5), whose true epsilon at the same delta is 11.480022787731485 - a 2.62x under-report, with no warning or error. Every other strategy in the same call shape scales correctly at the same (n=1000, min_sep=100, k=5) point: band_mf 1.00000 -> 2.23607 (exactly sqrt(5)), bsr 1.12413 -> 2.51364, lambda_cgd 1.00000 -> 2.23607, bisr 1.00000 -> 2.69449, blt 1.78601 -> 4.43081; identity alone stays at 1.00000 -> 1.00000. A mitigating prose caveat exists at docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280, but that same sentence is now wrong about BandMF (see the companion finding), so a reader who notices the BandMF half is stale has reason to discount the Identity half too.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_identity.py:45-46 - `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float:` / `return 1.0`; class docstring :22 asserts "sensitivity == 1 for any horizon".
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/types.py:55-59 - the post-e44d6ab6 protocol docstring declaring the Identity exemption legitimate.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_band_mf.py:138-187 - the converted sibling: k = minsep_true_max_participations(...); if k == 1 return coefs.norm(); else sqrt(minsep_sensitivity_upper_bound(...)).

Measured on this tree (12146ec4, native rebuilt from source): sensitivity ratios sens(min_sep=100,k=5)/sens(k=1) are identity 1.0000, band_mf 2.2361, bsr 2.2361, lambda_cgd 2.2361, bisr 2.6945, blt 2.4808 (sqrt(5) = 2.2361); reported eps 4.37717809602987 vs correct 11.480022787731485 (da.gaussian(1.0/sqrt(5)).epsilon_at(1e-5)).
findings.fix_sketch: Give IdentityStrategy the same schema-aware sensitivity as its siblings: `def sensitivity(self, *, n_steps, min_sep=1, max_participations=None) -> float: return math.sqrt(minsep_true_max_participations(n=n_steps, min_sep=min_sep, max_participations=max_participations))` - for C = I the exact Theorem-2 value is sqrt(k), and _toeplitz.minsep_sensitivity_squared on the coefficient vector [1, 0, ..., 0] already returns k, so it can simply delegate. Verify the three amplified call sites are unaffected: CyclicPoisson never calls sensitivity for Identity (_poisson.py:190-192 sets effective_nm = nm directly), BallsInBins uses sigma_eff = nm/sqrt(num_epochs) (_balls_in_bins.py:190-197), and _second_moment.py:140-145 asks for min_sep=n_steps/max_participations=1 which still yields 1.0. If a fix is deferred, make it fail closed instead of fail open: raise from IdentityStrategy.sensitivity when minsep_true_max_participations(...) > 1, and drop the "may ignore the schema" clause at types.py:55-59.

findings.title: Reference and user-guide accounting docs still claim bare BandMF sensitivity accounts for one participation, contradicting the code and band-mf.md after #998
findings.claim: Both files say "Bare BandMF and Identity sensitivity currently accounts for one participation. Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation." Commit e44d6ab6 made BandMfStrategy.sensitivity schema-aware (_band_mf.py:138-187), so the BandMF half is false, and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md - updated in the same commit - says the opposite twice: :74-76 ("band_mf_strategy(...).sensitivity(n_steps=..., min_sep=..., max_participations=...) returns this value [S = kappa*sqrt(k')]; pass min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 to ask for kappa instead") and :181-186 ("Pass the participation schema you actually run under ... because the bare PLD is calibrated to the schema sensitivity S"). The Identity half is still true - and this one sentence is the only place the Identity limitation is documented at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Two readers get opposite answers from the shipped docs for the same API call. A reader of docs/reference/accounting.md avoids bare BandMF multi-participation accounting that now works correctly (a utility cost, conservative). Worse for privacy: a reader who checks band-mf.md, finds the reference sentence contradicted for BandMF, and concludes the sentence is stale, loses the only published warning about IdentityStrategy - the case that genuinely still under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k) (companion finding). Reproduced: band_mf_strategy(bands=100).sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) = 2.23607 against 1.00000 at k=1, i.e. the reference sentence is measurably false for BandMF on this tree.
evidence: docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 - verbatim identical sentence.
docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:74-76 and :181-186 - the contradicting, correct description, added by the same commit that changed the code.
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_band_mf.py:138-187 - schema-aware sensitivity with the k == 1 shortcut, so only an explicit min_sep=n_steps/max_participations=1 returns kappa.
git show e44d6ab6 --stat - touches docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md but neither docs/reference/accounting.md nor docs/user-guide/accounting.md.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the sentence in both files with two separate statements: bare BandMF/BLT/BSR/BISR/lambda-CGD sensitivity honours (min_sep, max_participations) and must be given the schema actually run; bare IdentityStrategy still prices one participation and must not be used to budget repeated participation until _identity.py:45 is fixed. Link docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md#privacy-analysis from the reference entry so the two cannot drift apart again.

Migration narrative belongs in PR bodies and the changelog." It also sits at the root of a repository whose Marble milestone was public-release readiness, next to README.md, SECURITY.md and LICENSE, where a reader will take it for project documentation.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone browsing the repository root sees a file that reads like a design document but is a point-in-time research snapshot with statements already stale (it describes work "as pending" that has since merged), and its roadmap language ("follow-up work", "not a condition for closing #795") is indistinguishable from a commitment. findings.title: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md carries issue-tracker and roadmap narrative in a user-facing mechanism reference
findings.claim: The BISR execution section added by d09d7b9a tells the user which GitHub issue the design satisfies and what work is not being done: "This bounded ring is the complete `O(p)` execution design required by [issue #795](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/issues/795)." and "PRNG replay could trade that persistent tensor storage for extra noise generation, but replay and a reusable generic banded-inverse executor are follow-up directions rather than requirements for this bounded BISR path." AGENTS.md says user-facing docs describe the current API and behavior, not development history, and that "Forward-references to features that don't yet exist in the codebase don't belong anywhere". The factual half of the same section (bounded window, O(min(p, n_steps) * model_size), the explicit formula, the checkpoint-layout warning) is accurate and should stay - I verified all of it numerically.
findings.failure_scenario: A user reading the mechanism reference to decide whether BISR fits their memory budget is handed an internal issue number and a roadmap sentence instead of a straight statement of the current cost, and must follow a tracker link to a private-issue URL to understand what the paragraph is asserting. The forward reference also reads as a commitment that a PRNG-replay BISR is planned.
evidence: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:112-118 (added by d09d7b9a) - the issue link and the follow-up-directions sentence.
AGENTS.md, section Documentation - diary-free rule and the forward-reference prohibition.

The neighbouring factual claims are correct and were verified: state is min(p, n_steps)-1 pytrees (measured 3 buffers / 600,000 bytes at bandwidth=4 for n_steps in {64, 256, 1024}), and the released noise matches the dense reference to 3.7e-15 relative over 418 configurations.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the formula, the O(min(p, n_steps) * model_size) statement and the checkpoint-layout warning; delete the issue link and the follow-up-directions paragraph. If a memory/compute trade-off note is wanted, state it as a present-tense property ("BISR trades bandwidth for retained noise buffers; raise bandwidth only while the retained pytrees fit") with no tracker reference.

Scope: packages/opaque-dpftrl (all 25 delta commits touching it: git log --oneline 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- packages/opaque-dpftrl), plus the DP-FTRL-owned surfaces those commits reach in packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py + _training_arguments.py and in packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/{_base.py,composition/_cached.py,composition/_iter_cache_key.py,composition/_per_step.py} where the DP-FTRL fixes landed. Per-commit coverage. Read in full and traced: f2d90d61 (#1018 lambda-CGD stream namespacing), d09d7b9a (#886 BISR bounded state), 4bfd0c16 (#883 schedule identity in composition), 87404a1b (#894 remove horizon prefix accounting -- pld_at/PerStep/per_step/atomic_unit/CachedProcess horizon warning all deleted; checked for dangling references across packages/, docs/, examples/, tests/), 79acf31d (#1022 require explicit horizons for bare MF), e44d6ab6 (#998 honour the participation schema in BandMF sensitivity), e89e858a (#858 constrain BLTs to the min-sep sensitivity domain), e87a0c21 (#857 harden signed-encoder accounting: BISR/lambda-CGD lr_schedule tombstones, |C| gram construction, inv_coefficients validation), dd65957d (#884 namespace sampler RNG streams), 1794504b (#901 MFNoiseState serializer), 3b22a6af (#850 generalized Poisson PLD, dpftrl-side call change only), 280e4969 (#853 sample_rate=1.0), 20dd47aa (#881 random-allocation epoch memoisation), fc44ec8d (#761 k-out-of-t unification, dpftrl-side references), 7b26f655 (#760 exception taxonomy -- verified ConfigurationError/InputTypeError still subclass ValueError/TypeError, but noted that several ValueError/TypeError sites became CheckpointError, which is a RuntimeError and no longer a ValueError/TypeError: _strategy_codec.py:56,68,120,143,173). Skimmed (test-only or pinning): eb6da40b, 76fd4e3e, 4867feb1, 31ffed65, acb83d1a, e88c5ea9, 8f8903b7, 43fc883d, 2ecc00a8, 12146ec4.

Executions performed (native extension rebuilt from the current tree with `cargo build --release -p opaque-accounting --features python-extension`, since the installed editable .so predated the delta and made bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle signature-incompatible):
- Full dpftrl suite: 620 passed, 18 deselected (-m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed').
- dpftrl DDP/Gloo suite: 5 passed (-m 'distributed and not cuda').
- BISR direct-vs-dense equivalence: 418 configurations (bandwidth 2/3/4/6/12 x n_steps 1..256 x normalized x momentum 0/0.5/0.9/0.99, plus three signed non-monotone custom inv_coefficients sets), worst relative error 3.680e-15; realized noise_stddev vs streaming_matrix.row_norms_squared matched to <1e-9 across a separate grid; state size flat at min(p,n_steps)-1 buffers; resume bit-exact.
- lambda-CGD stream: byte-level check that step-0 noise no longer equals split(key,2)[0] or fold_in(key,0) draws and does equal the mf_gaussian_column-rooted draw.
- Composition identity: b_min_sep and cyclic_poisson BandMF processes with linear/exponential/no lr_schedule -- direct, reversed, right-spine and CachedProcess merges all Composed for differing schedules, Repeated for identical.
- acc.cached on a DP-FTRL accountant: no RuntimeWarning, CachedProcess actually installed, epsilon unchanged.
- CyclicPoisson(identity) vs DP-SGD repeat(poisson(gaussian)) agreement at four (nm,q,T) points, exact.
- b-min-sep MC determinism under RAYON_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,4,8}: identical float64 epsilon.
- Sensitivity-domain sweep after e89e858a removed skip_checks: BLT (max_buffers 1..10 x momentum 1.0/0.9/0.5/0.0) and BSR (bandwidth/alpha/beta grid) and BandMF over five participation contexts -- 0 exceptions, so the newly strict minsep_sensitivity_squared domain does not reject legal configurations. Reviewed minsep_sensitivity_upper_bound (_toeplitz.py:520-556) and confirmed the reverse-cumulative-max majorant plus triangle inequality is a sound upper bound for signed/non-monotone columns.
- BISR compute-dtype guard (_validate_effective_runtime_coefficients) across fp16/bf16/fp32 x n_steps up to 1e7 x bandwidth 4/16 x normalized: no false rejections.

Areas deliberately not re-derived: the Rust b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio (OPQ-300 / #779) and the internals of 3b22a6af's generalized Poisson operator, both of which live in packages/opaque-accounting and belong to the accounting reviewer; I verified only the dpftrl-facing behaviour of each (thread determinism, and exact agreement of CyclicPoisson-identity with the DP-SGD Poisson composition). Trainer-side items reviewed only insofar as they gate DP-FTRL: the OPQ-320 stop-at-epsilon carve-out at _dp_trainer.py:1246-1253 survives, but the configuration it exposed (whole-horizon mechanism + fixed privacy_noise_multiplier + privacy_target_epsilon) is now rejected at construction by _training_arguments.py:1241-1257, so the overshoot is unreachable; the horizon branch at _dp_trainer.py:4216-4224 is correspondingly dead-but-guarded. Sampler cross-version resume was checked and is safe: dd65957d's _from_stream_key classmethods (packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../sampling/_b_min_sep.py:68-87, _balls_in_bins.py:92-111) bypass the new fold on restore, so a pre-namespacing checkpoint reconstructs the same bin assignment / Markov chain it was written with.

Result: all eight Bazalt items in my area verified fixed (six fixed-verified, two fixed-by-removal with the removal confirmed complete and reference-clean); two adjacent accounting items spot-verified; one not verified and reported as such. Four new findings, one of them epsilon-affecting.
